body:
Clap propagated the global default port into deployment arguments, so `router deploy --config FILE` planned port 8080 instead of the configured listener. Docker's dependency layer also omitted the declared `hot_paths` bench, causing both 1.16.0 image builds to fail after stable release publication had already succeeded.

This restores config/flag parity, expands home paths on the selected target, refuses a host listener mismatch without a start plan, and keeps future releases as prereleases until every required artifact is verified. Local, host and staging operations also share an explicit unlock guard, fixing the macOS lifecycle retry race exposed by CI.

Fixes #687

Fixes #688

Fixes #689

## Requirements and implementation

| Requirement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Docker can parse every declared target | Generate disposable targets from Cargo.toml, including custom paths; remove stubs, copy real targets and invalidate their cached builds. Regressions cover benches, tests, examples, custom paths/extensions, both flat and directory default layouts, package-named binaries and the current manifest. |
| Usable amd64/arm64 release images | Preserve both native architecture builds and both registries. The Fixed changelog fragment triggers the next patch release after merge. |
| Complete artifacts before stable/latest and crates.io | Prepare a GitHub prerelease; publish the crate and promote stable/latest only after binaries, both registries' manifests, provenance and lifecycle checks succeed. Recovery/delivery checks treat prereleases as incomplete. |
| Docker regression check on PRs | A path-filtered workflow builds the complete amd64 runtime without pushing, then runs all three shipped command names. |
| Default image preflight before planning | Check a cached image or registry manifest before default local-container plans and staging startup. Missing versions report `image-unpublished`, the version and `--image`/`--build` remedies; registry connectivity/authentication failures remain distinct. Explicit image/build overrides bypass the default-image preflight, credential refusals retain precedence, and staging status/verification remains independent of image availability. |
| Every applicable config field equals flags | Real-binary tables cover `[deploy]`/`[local]` in host/container modes and shared remote fields. Config-only startup verifies the actual HTTP listener and convergence. Explicit CLI values, including 8080, and ROUTER_PORT keep precedence. |
| Clear `~` root semantics | Expand local/staging roots with the caller's home, remote roots with the target user's home; retain config-relative ordinary paths and refuse unsupported `~user`. |
| A serving host on a different port blocks mutation | Report `port-mismatch`, suppress mutation steps and preserve the running PID and healthy original listener on status and deployment attempts. |
| One PR with separate closing references and a complete audit | Both child issues and all comments were read; all requirements, alternatives, sources and scope findings are recorded in the linked investigation. |

[Detailed analysis, solution alternatives, online sources and test plan](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-689-4bcc94b199c2/dev/log/issues/689/pulls/690/README.md).

Existing components considered include cargo-chef, clap ValueSource, shellexpand, Docker manifest inspection and gh release promotion. The implementation uses clap/Docker's existing facilities and a small standard-library TOML generator rather than adding application dependencies.

## Reproduction and regression tests

- Before the fixes, a real CLI run with `[local] mode = "host", port = 18080` rendered listener 8080; the same occurred under `[deploy]`. The config-only host test now starts on the configured ephemeral port, answers health checks and converges without replacing its PID.
- A root of `~/Data/router-host` previously resolved underneath the config directory. Real-CLI and remote-agent tests now verify caller/target home expansion without creating directories during status.
- The host mismatch test originally printed a start step and the old blocker name; it now verifies `port-mismatch`, no start step and unchanged PID/health.
- The Docker experiment originally failed because target generation was absent. It now parses the repository manifest and compiles a dependency-free manifest with every target category before and after replacing cache stubs. A final failing regression also exposed valid `name/main.rs` targets being rejected after source copy; the helper now resolves both Cargo default layouts, including package-named binaries.
- Release regressions originally failed because preparation published crates.io immediately and no PR Docker workflow existed. They now enforce prerelease preparation, the final artifact gate and the no-push runtime check.
- A fake-Docker real-CLI regression originally reached planning with the missing default image. It now fails before planning or creating the deployment root, including staging.
- A final compatibility regression originally rejected staging `--build` with `image-unpublished`. Both local and staging explicit builds now bypass registry preflight; the real-CLI test verifies no manifest probe and that staging reaches execution.
- The macOS CI log showed a completed operation still blocking the next retry at `deploy_local_secret_tests.rs:[REDACTED] A deterministic test originally failed with `WouldBlock` while retaining a copied descriptor after dropping the operation. The shared guard now unlocks explicitly; the regression also verifies that an active owner still excludes competitors.
- The Windows log exposed one workflow assertion using raw CRLF text. A retained experiment reproduced that failure on Linux; the assertion now uses the existing normalization helper, and all 29 release workflow/gate tests pass with LF and CRLF inputs.

## Validation and publication limits

- Local: formatting; all-target/all-feature Clippy with warnings denied; file-size, terminology, release-workflow and workflow-tool checks; actionlint; Docker manifest/cache experiments; path and release script tests.
- The complete local binary/integration run passes 1,086 tests across 104 targets (one opt-in test ignored), including the lifecycle-lock and staging-build corrections. The stricter table also passes using only config/status, with its fixture image stored in the file. Doc tests pass; the portable remote-agent parity suite also passes separately. Full library, binary and integration suites also pass on Linux, macOS and Windows in CI on final commit `ac47555`.
- All six workflows passed on `ac47555cd44f2c0f84cf7915e7e96d7c4b7c63e1`: 19 successful checks and 10 intentionally skipped jobs. Results: [CI/CD, all platforms, coverage and package build](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248373), [Docker runtime and all shipped commands](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248389), [fuzzing](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248414), [benchmarks](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248214), [real-client capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248482), and [macOS Keychain](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37353248577). Final coverage is 86.03%, and CI leaves the committed baseline unchanged.
- This workspace has a 3 GB memory cap. The full library unit-test crate exceeds it during code generation even with one job, no debug symbols/incremental compilation and serialized LLVM. The diagnostic experiment and logs are preserved; full-suite validation uses CI without changing production or CI compiler flags.
- The staging regression raised coverage to 86.029112% (71,750 / 83,402 lines). The automatic ratchet required that measured baseline to be committed; its threshold check passed, and the full CI report verifies the corrected baseline locally.
- Remote defaults already build the exact release source tag on the target; the issue's claim that every remote default pulls GHCR was not reproducible. That existing behavior is preserved. Remote-only server/credential settings retain their documented context rather than redirecting local deployments.
- The previously reported second writer was not reproduced: existing host assessment already refused the mutation. The misleading start plan and blocker name are corrected and protected by a real-process regression.
- Publishing repaired stable images requires merging this PR and completing the default-branch release pipeline. This PR prepares the next patch trigger and does not rewrite the existing release/tag history.
